fiserv. Internship Interview Experience
SIDDHARTH SHAH, B.TECH CS 23’
siddharthsshah1207@gmail.com
Group Discussion (30 mins): September 30, 2021
(Nearly 50 students were there in this round)
Fiserv was the only company to start with a GD. There was no Coding Test.
We were divided into groups of 6 and each group was called in different meetings for the
session. The panelist introduced himself and gave us the topic for GD. For my group it was,
‘Will Crypto succeed or fail?’. They gave everyone 1-2 minutes to think and then we were
asked to start.
Tips for GD:
●
There is no particular order in which you have to speak unless given by the panelist. It is
recommended to be the first one to start the discussion, it shows initiative.
●
Keep your points valid and crisp. The panelist comes to know if you are blabbering stuff
or repeating others’ points
●
Adding real time examples in your discussion would be great
●
Even if you have a lot of unique content to speak, make sure it isn’t so long that the
panelist has to stop you to give others a chance
●
Be a patient listener and listen to each and every thing that others speak. Sometimes it
might give you new points to add to your content.
●
NEVER interrupt when someone else is speaking. It is a discussion and not a debate
●
You can contradict someone when it is your turn, but do it in a respectful manner
●
You can also smartly summarize the entire discussion if you are one of the last guys to
speak(and you don’t have any new insights to give), but this should be your last resort
●
It is not necessary that you will be asked to speak only once. Everyone might be asked to
speak multiple times depending on the time constraint. For my group, we asked to speak
twice
1

Technical Interview (20-25 mins): October 1, 2021
(Almost everyone were shortlisted for this round, 44 people were there in this round)
The interviewer was extremely friendly. To make me comfortable, he started by asking me
things like What time did you wake up? Did you have breakfast? Do you exercise?
He then asked me to introduce myself to start with the main discussion.
I had mentioned about a Smart City designing competition on my resume. He found it
pretty interesting and we had a quite long discussion on that.
He asked me what it was exactly and what was my role in the competition. Based on the
discussion, he gave me a scenario for a city and asked me how I would take care of the
environment while planning the infrastructure of the city.
(These set of questions might seem weird but he asked me only because it was on my resume)
He moved on to the Technical questions:
●
He asked me about my proficiency in C++ and asked me to rate myself out of 10. (I
said 7-8). He asked me to explain Arrays, some twisted questions on array
declaration and how space will actually be blocked in the memory
●
Some basic questions on Object oriented programming which i don't remember
exactly but they were quite manageable
●
He asked me about the Storage Classes in C. I was not very much sure about the
term ‘Storage Classes’, so I confirmed with him first whether I am on the right track
●
Explain the difference between sizeof and STL length function. As a follow up
question, he gave me a char array which is not completely filled and asked about the
respective outputs
●
For DSA, he asked me a question on Double Ended Queue. The question was:
Given a Double Ended Queue, how will you delete any given node from the queue
(Only the approach was expected here, not the code)
Always ask questions at the end of the interview. I asked about the work I will get to do in
terms of technology, since Fiserv is a Fin-Tech company and also about the tech stack they
use
2

HR Round (35-40 mins): October 1,2021
(Around 30 people were shortlisted for this round)
This interview will be taken by a senior manager but there is nothing to worry about. This
round was even more friendly than the previous one. This round did not feel like an
interview at all, it was an extremely casual conversation. This round is intended to gain
some insight into the candidate, about his/her work choices, preferences, approaches,
personality, life experiences etc. There were a lot of random things we talked about but
some which I remember are:
●
Introduction and hobbies, the manager also talked about what he likes to do and
how we had similar hobbies
●
He asked me if I had been to Pune (since they have a office over there) and how was
my experience staying there
●
He asked me which domains of technology I like to work in and asked me to talk
about any project I had worked on. He was more interested in the architecture
working behind the scenes
●
He was interested in something  like some gateways or APIs if I had used in the
project
●
He asked me some Technical questions as well. He was not really testing me but
wanted to get to know my understanding of technical stuff
○
He asked me if I understand how things work when we try to make a
payment from a bank account to Amazon. I explained him roughly but he
was expecting things like Payment Gateways and APIs
○
He asked me if I understood Agile technologies and Software Engineering
models to which I said I don’t have much knowledge about it
○
Then he asked me to give my approaches on very beginner C questions. They
were very simple Arithmetic questions
At the end, I asked him about Fiserv as a company and about his journey and experience
with Fiserv
3

23 of us were offered the internship which was surprisingly high!
(Only 10 were selected in 2020)
[We had to wait for 4 days for the results which was a much bigger task :P]
PREPARATION:
Internship Interview Preparation Resources
GENERAL TIPS:
●
Do some basic research about the company and refer to all Past experiences. It will
help you understand what type of an interview it is going to be
●
For Fiserv particularly, it is a company which won't go hard on you in Coding aspects.
They are more interested in judging your analytical approaches and on-toes thinking
along with what you have done apart from academics
●
Always keep your basics strong
●
NEVER lie on your resume or during an interview because if you fail to prove
yourself, it will be a big hurdle for you
●
Also don’t oversell yourself on your resume because they might raise the level of
questions to test your real aptitude and you might fail to meet their expectations
●
If you are unsure about any question, straight away tell them. It is completely
acceptable and won’t harm you in any way
●
Be alert enough to drive the discussion in some other direction if you foresee that
the interviewer is jumping on a topic you are not very good at
●
Thoroughly prepare for every sentence written on your resume, writing down your
speech will surely help
●
Don’t hesitate to ask if you don't understand a question, in fact clearing things out
creates a good impression. Discuss what you are thinking on a question with the
interviewer
●
Be Confident & Natural Always and ensure you are throwing a decent cheerful
image of yourself
GOOD LUCK!!!
